quiz.q: Forty erroneous bits touch twenty symbols in one RS(544,514) codeword. What follows?
opts: They exceed the guaranteed 15-symbol correction capacity
quiz.why: Twenty erroneous symbols exceed the guaranteed capacity. Beyond fifteen, successful correction is not guaranteed; the outcome and failure detection depend on the error pattern and decoder requirements.

quiz.q: Can the optical PMD's BER allocation be used as the pass limit for an AUI?
opts: Yes, all segments share one limit
No, use the allocation for that interface and reference configuration
Yes, if the MAC rate is unchanged
Only when no frames are lost
quiz.why: The reference architecture assigns different contributions to optical and electrical segments. The applicable specification defines the observation point and limit; a shared outer code does not make those limits interchangeable.

quiz.q: A link reports zero frame loss during a measurement. What does that establish?

quiz.why: FEC can repair errors while leaving no post-FEC loss. Use pre-FEC and corrected-error measurements, with signal and lane status, to assess how much degradation the link might tolerate.

quiz.q: Why does an intermediate FEC termination need defined error propagation?
opts: Residual wrong data can be re-encoded into a valid next-segment codeword
quiz.why: Re-encoding residual wrong data does not expose the earlier damage to the next decoder's parity checks. Detected failures must be signalled across the boundary according to the architecture's rules.

quiz.q: What does Gray coding guarantee for a nearest-neighbor PAM4 decision error?
opts: Only one of the two mapped bits changes
quiz.why: Adjacent levels have labels differing in one bit. This reduces bit damage for those transitions, but does not necessarily halve Reed-Solomon symbol errors: one or two wrong bits within the same ten-bit symbol still count as one erroneous symbol.

opts: To give each side measurable requirements for the connector interface
quiz.why: Defined reference points let host and module implementations be assessed against compatible requirements. Their vendors need not be different, and interoperability testing can still be required.

quiz.q: What should be checked before using a host and module for LPO?
opts: Their compatible linear-interface requirements and complete-link qualification
quiz.why: Ordinary retimed-interface compliance is not a substitute for the requirements of a linear link. Linear-interface specifications exist, and qualification must cover the intended host, module, channel and operating conditions.

quiz.q: Why do OSFP-XD cages include keying features?
opts: To prevent incompatible modules being inserted
quiz.why: OSFP and OSFP-XD have different module interfaces. Keying protects against incompatible insertion; it does not establish a module's optical capabilities.
